Description of Assessment Instrument Students in the Data Analytics for Accounting and Auditing Certificate program are assessed on their data analytics skills via the course projects in MAC 511, MAC 512, MAC 518. The projects allow students to choose any accounting or auditing related problem that you are interested in. Students are then required to find a related dataset and perform data analytics according to the following process: 1) Define the accounting or auditing related question that can be answered by the data; 2) Master the data by downloading, validating, cleaning, and importing it to the analytics tools (if not excel); 3) Perform appropriate analysis approach to the data to find the answer of your question; 4) Address and refine results using appropriate visualizations; 5) Communicate your analysis process and results in a written report and an oral presentation. Description of Assessment Method (Rubric attached) The project reports as well as the oral presentations will be assessed by two independent assessors using a rubric that consisted of five criteria and three levels of expectation. The five criteria are: 1) Identify the questions; 2) Master the data; 3) Perform test plan; 4) Address and refine results; and 5) Communicate insights and track outcomes. The three levels of expectations were 1) Unsatisfactory, 2) Satisfactory, and 3) Exemplary.

To avoid conflict with Federal legislation regarding Title IX and the Board of Trustees Policy on Sexual Harrassment Manual language must be clear that the University follows procedures and policies in the the BOT Policy on Sexual harrassment in such cases Motion: Delete language addressing sexual harrassment in 5.74.20 in Chapter 5 and add language that clearly states that the cases involving sexual misconduct shall follow procedures accommpanying the Board of Trustees’ Policy on Sexual Misconduct, and change standard of proof to align with University Student Conduct System Standard of Proof.
Chapter 5 5.74.20 Hearing Panels.
For each case to be adjudicated, a hearing panel shall be drawn from the Conduct Board.

Panel members shall be appointed from the Conduct Board members by the Dean of Students Office, Office of Community Standards.
Faculty or staff who have been Conduct Board members in the past and who are conversant with the current system may be asked to serve on individual hearing panels when a sufficient number of current Conduct Board members are not available.
For non-academic cases, each panel shall comprise one student member, one faculty and one staff member.
In cases where faculty or staff are unavailable, two faculty or two staff members would be sufficient.
For academic cases involving undergraduate students, each panel shall comprise two faculty members and one undergraduate student member.
For academic cases involving graduate students, each panel shall comprise two faculty members and one graduate student member.
For cases involving sexual misconduct and relationship violence involving undergraduate students each panel shall comprise three faculty and/or staff members.
Each hearing panel shall also have an advisor, to be appointed by the Dean of Students.
The role of the advisor, who shall not be considered as a member of the panel, is spelled out in 9.21.10.

Cases involving sexual misconduct, sexual harassment or relationship violence that meet the applicable definitions of Title IX shall follow the procedures accompanying the Board of Trustees Policy on Sexual Misconduct .
For cases involving sexual misconduct and relationship violence not under the juristiction of Title IX and involving undergraduate students each panel shall comprise three faculty and/or staff members. #04-05–32 #05-06–2E , #18-19-6 Chapter 9 Student Activities

9.21.21 Presence of Accused, Oaths, Burden of Proof, and Standards of Proof. The accused must be present at the hearing (except as provided in 9.21.26). The charging official and the chair of the panel will work to eliminate preconduct and irrelevant information. If the charged student feels that this has not been done, the accused may add a written complaint or correction to the materials that are given to the hearing panel or officer. When the charged student denies responsibility, the burden of proof shall rest upon the person(s) bringing the charges. The standard for this proof shall be clear and convincing preponderance of the evidence. #04-05–32, #21-22-6
